description: A second-year Computer Science major who gained extensive C++ experience through personal systems programming projects and is now looking to formalize their understanding of algorithm efficiency.

nodes.title: C++ Foundations & Classes
nodes.description: Comprehensive overview of C++ classes, references, and manual memory management basics.
nodes.personalizationRationale: As a student with strong_prior_exposure, you will move quickly through these core C++ syntax requirements to ensure baseline consistency with the course text.

nodes.description: Advanced study of Resource Acquisition Is Initialization (RAII), move semantics, and template metaprogramming for efficient data structures.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Your strong_prior_exposure allows us to replace basic scaffolding with enrichment in high-performance C++ idioms and template depth.
nodes.title: Advanced C++: RAII & Templates

nodes.personalizationRationale: Because of your strong_prior_exposure, we focus on the rigorous C++ implementation of OOD patterns required for the cumulative course assignments.
nodes.description: Object-Oriented Design principles in C++, including inheritance hierarchies, polymorphism, and exception handling.
nodes.title: OOD: Inheritance & Exceptions
Arrays & Linked List Implementation
nodes.personalizationRationale: While you have strong_prior_exposure, mastering the textbook-specific pointer-based implementations is essential for the exam.
nodes.description: Implementation of Singly and Doubly Linked Lists in C++ and their application in memory management.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Asymptotic analysis is a core requirement for all students; your prior exposure provides a strong foundation for these theoretical proofs.
nodes.description: Introduction to Big-O, Omega, and Theta notations and the analysis of recursive algorithm complexity.
nodes.title: Recursion & Big-O Notation
Quiz 1: Recursion & Analysis
nodes.description: Proctored quiz covering recursion depth and the formal analysis of algorithmic performance.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This assessment ensures that your strong_prior_exposure translates into the specific mathematical rigor required by this course.
The course requires proficiency in these sequence structures; your prior knowledge will help you grasp the trade-offs between backends quickly.
nodes.description: Abstract Data Types (ADTs) for Stacks and Queues using both array-based and linked-list backends.
nodes.title: Stacks & Queues ADTs
Vectors & Iterators
nodes.description: Modern C++ vector implementation, iterator patterns, and the generic Sequence ADT.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Given your strong_prior_exposure, you can focus on the STL-like iterator mechanics that are central to the midterm exam.

nodes.title: Sequences & Bubble Sort
nodes.description: In-depth analysis of Bubble Sort within the context of sequence-based structures.
nodes.personalizationRationale: All students must understand the performance characteristics of basic sorting on sequence containers.

nodes.description: A cumulative review session covering all material from Block 01 through Block 03 in preparation for the midterm.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This mandatory checkpoint validates your understanding of foundational structures before the high-stakes midterm exam.
nodes.title: Midterm Performance Review

nodes.description: Hierarchical structures, tree terminology, and standard traversal algorithms (Pre, Post, and In-order).
nodes.personalizationRationale: Tree structures are new to many students; your strong_prior_exposure in programming logic will help you implement these recursive traversals.
nodes.title: General Trees & Traversals

nodes.personalizationRationale: Mastering binary trees is a core requirement for all students as they lead directly into balanced search trees.
nodes.description: Binary tree properties, height-balance fundamentals, and linked representation.
nodes.title: Binary Tree Mechanics
Priority Queues & Heaps
nodes.personalizationRationale: Heaps are a fundamental part of the cumulative syllabus and are heavily tested on the final exam.
nodes.description: Priority Queue ADT and its efficient implementation using the Heap data structure (up-heap/down-heap).

nodes.title: Maps & Hash Tables
nodes.personalizationRationale: Even with strong_prior_exposure, understanding the mathematical basis of hash functions is critical for the required course assignments.
nodes.description: Hash functions, collision resolution strategies, and the Map/Dictionary ADT.

nodes.personalizationRationale: This quiz serves as a key checkpoint for the complex material in the latter half of the semester.
nodes.description: Assessment focusing on hashing performance and dictionary interface design.
nodes.title: Quiz 3: Hashing & Maps

nodes.description: Binary Search Tree (BST) operations and the mechanics of AVL tree rotations for height balancing.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Your strong_prior_exposure in logic will be beneficial as you navigate the theoretical proofs of AVL balance.
nodes.title: BSTs & AVL Trees

nodes.description: Properties and implementation of (2,4) trees and Red-Black trees.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Multi-way search trees are a core required topic that demands high conceptual precision for the final exam.
nodes.title: Red-Black & Multi-Way Trees
Merge & Selection Sort Analysis
nodes.personalizationRationale: Sorting algorithms are a capstone requirement that tests your ability to apply Big-O analysis to practical logic.
nodes.description: Formal analysis of Merge Sort and Selection Sort, including divide-and-conquer strategy proofs.

nodes.title: Capstone: Data Structure Synthesis
nodes.description: Synthesis of all course topics, comparing the efficiency of every data structure covered throughout the term.
nodes.personalizationRationale: The capstone review ensures you can integrate your strong_prior_exposure with the specific theoretical frameworks taught this semester.
This final assessment ensures you are fully prepared for the cumulative final exam, which accounts for 30% of your grade.
nodes.description: Comprehensive final review session covering the entire course syllabus in preparation for the final exam.
nodes.title: Final Cumulative Review
